findings.claim: The record says every cluster an adopter runs installs Kyverno from the adopter's file, "its named cluster and its drift lane". It treats kind-driftwood as the only named cluster with an engine. But tuppence and ludlow each have their own named cluster, and no Kyverno runs on either one. So item 3 of ticket 147 quietly adds a new engine install to two clusters that have none. The Done line checks only kind-driftwood, so it does not match item 3. The CONTEXT definition ("the engine version an adopter's clusters run") is false for kind-tuppence and kind-ludlow today.
findings.evidence: tuppence and ludlow scripts/lib.sh:5 set CLUSTER=tuppence and CLUSTER=ludlow (ctx kind-tuppence and kind-ludlow). Their scripts/up.sh:20-26 install Flux only, and gotk-sync.yaml:47 reconciles ./gitops/apps. tuppence and ludlow .github/workflows/drift-sample.yml:55-56 say: "the local kind-tuppence [kind-ludlow] cluster carries neither ... the engine exists only on this ephemeral cluster". verify-reconcile.sh:152-153 in both skips on "Kyverno MutatingPolicy CRD not installed". Hub talk/up.sh:82-86 runs those scripts. talk/up.sh:66 runs platform engine/up.sh, which sets CTX default kind-driftwood at :12. talk/up.sh:76-77 puts tuppence's flagship on kind-driftwood.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to ticket 147's Today section that kind-tuppence and kind-ludlow run no Kyverno. Then decide decision 17's scope; it is delegated under ADR-0025. One option: "every cluster that runs an engine installs it from the file". The other: talk/up.sh adds Kyverno to kind-tuppence and kind-ludlow. Make ADR-0033 point 2, CONTEXT Declared engine and ticket 147's Done say the same thing.

findings.claim: "Prefer an adopter whose named cluster no other adopter uses ... Today driftwood and tuppence share kind-driftwood" names the wrong test. tuppence's named cluster is kind-tuppence, and no other adopter uses it. What tuppence shares is kind-driftwood, where its workload flagship runs. Read literally, the rule lets tuppence be chosen.
findings.evidence: tuppence scripts/lib.sh:5 sets CLUSTER=tuppence. tuppence reset/up.sh:12 sets CTX="${CTX:-kind-driftwood}". Hub talk/up.sh:76-77 runs "tuppence: workload flagship" on the driftwood substrate.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the rule to: prefer an adopter none of whose workloads run on a cluster another adopter uses (today, ludlow).

findings.claim: The record says some machinery bodies "build the same variables.tier label map that does not compile on 1.19.1". Exactly two machinery bodies build that label map, and in both variables.tier is the string literal 'isolated', not cage-tier's dyn-typed conditional. In this run, both bodies compiled and mutated on Kyverno 1.19.1 under the offline CLI.
findings.evidence: driftwood composed/orphan-cage.yaml:26-27,33 and composed/governed-namespace-guard.yaml:29-30,36; platform distribution/versions.yaml:261-262,268 and :330-331,337 hold `- name: tier / expression: '''isolated'''`. policy/v5.0.0 cage-tier.yaml derives tier from namespaceObject labels. Run in this review (offline, not a committed capture), with the kyverno 1.19.1 darwin_arm64 binary (sha256 44477b11..., which matches captures-engine-versions.txt:14) applying both committed bodies: rc=0, "pass: 4, fail: 0, warn: 0, error: 0, skip: 4", both pods mutated to posture.acme.io/tier: isolated. 1.18.2 gives the same result. The other machinery bodies were not run.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the two bodies with their lines. Say that their tier is the literal 'isolated' and that they compile on 1.19.1 offline. Keep ticket 148 item 6 conditional on ticket 146's grade. Decision 16 does not change.

findings.claim: The record says ticket 89's register, NORTH-STAR.md:54 and ticket 84 each commit the posture-trust-boundary retirement to the next declared line. Ticket 84 never mentions posture-trust-boundary. Only the register does, and it names ticket 84 as the owner of the next line. So two records commit the retirement, not three.
findings.evidence: grep -i 'trust|posture' on .scratch/ecosystem/issues/84-being-behind-costs-something.md matches only the ticket title and unrelated "retirement" lines, never posture-trust-boundary. verify/deny-is-not-a-rung/register.yaml:169-193 says "the next declared line, which ticket 84 owns" and awaits "ticket 84's next declared policy line". NORTH-STAR.md:54 does commit it.
findings.suggested_fix: Say "ticket 89's register and NORTH-STAR.md:54 commit the retirement to the next declared line, which the register assigns to ticket 84". Decision 15 stands on those two records.

GitHub compare fd90931fad...v1.19.0 reports ahead, behind_by=0, so PR #16505's change is in 1.19.0. That makes the explanation plausible but leaves it unmeasured there.

findings.claim: The README says moving the bodies to v1 "gave the same results in every cell" and cites captures/f-v1-vs-v1alpha1-output-compare.txt. That capture itself marks one cell DIFFERS, and the README does not explain it.

Diffing a1-row-1.19.1 against f-v1-on-tagged-1.19.1 cage-tier.kyverno-test.out.txt shows the same compile error in both ("expected type 'string' but found 'dyn'"). findings.claim: Item 6 compares require-nonroot's PolicyReport entries "between the adopter's last 1.18.2 sample and its first 1.19.1 sample". Drift samples record no PolicyReport entries, so the last 1.18.2 sample has nothing to compare against.

findings.claim: "No adopter file names platform ./engine" is false. "Each adopter serves its own composed set (gitops/composed/)" holds only on the lane: on the named clusters, Flux reconciles ./gitops/apps only.

findings.suggested_fix: Write "no adopter's Flux reconciles a platform path". Say that tuppence's reset README names platform engine/up.sh for its flagship on kind-driftwood, and that gitops/composed reaches only the lane.
